cases.title: Ollama returns HTTP 500 for structured-output requests

groundTruth.cause: Inference on Ollama's ROCm GPU backend produced corrupted output, so the JSON-schema grammar rejected it ("Unexpected empty grammar stack") and requests failed with HTTP 500; forcing the Vulkan backend (HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1) fixed it. The "llama-server terminated" lines are runners being stopped on model unload or restart, not crashes.
goodNextSteps: Run the same request on another GPU backend (Vulkan via HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1) or on the CPU, to see whether the failures follow the ROCm backend
Retry without a JSON schema and check whether the raw output is corrupted (e.g. repeated "0") rather than just failing the grammar

answer.summary: Ollama returns HTTP 500 errors for structured-output requests due to either a parser stack failure or a llama-server termination during processing, with the former being more directly tied to the observed grammar stack exception and the latter potentially being a symptom of the same underlying issue.
missingEvidence: A diagnostic log from the llama-server process showing the exact stack trace or internal state at the time of the grammar stack failure
The command-line arguments or configuration used to start the llama-server instance during the incident

hypotheses.cause: The HTTP 500 errors are caused by a parsing failure in the grammar stack during structured-output processing, which occurs when the parser accepts an input piece but fails to maintain a valid stack state, leading to an unexpected empty stack condition.
hypotheses.nextStep: Retrieve the llama-server logs from the same time window as F1 and F2 (13:18:37 to 13:27:52) to inspect the internal parser state and identify where the grammar stack becomes empty.

hypotheses.cause: The HTTP 500 errors are triggered by the llama-server process terminating with exit status 1, which may be a downstream failure that interrupts structured output processing and results in a 500 response from the Ollama service.
hypotheses.nextStep: Check the startup configuration and command-line arguments of the llama-server process to determine if any malformed or invalid input was passed during structured-output requests.

answer.summary: The incident appears to stem from either memory exhaustion in the prompt cache or hardware instability on the AMD RX 7900 XT. The logs show growing memory usage and repeated exceptions during token processing, suggesting one or both of these root causes. A memory usage check and a hardware-specific test are recommended to confirm.
